summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around AI data-center photonics capacity. The clean two-lane map is: reference leaders COHR and LITE as established InP / laser / optical-component capacity anchors; FN as a direct manufacturing-platform beneficiary for optical interconnect scale-up; and ALMU as a small-cap speculative-shadow candidate tied to III-V-on-silicon photonics that could matter if native InP capacity remains structurally constrained. Claims are intentionally conservative because much of the available context comes from investment research snippets rather than primary filings. Layer 1B expands the universe around AI data-center photonics capacity. The node appears to be a plausible chokepoint because 800G/1.6T optical links, lasers, photodetectors, InP devices, and optical manufacturing capacity are increasingly tied to hyperscaler bandwidth demand. The cleanest reference names are Coherent and Lumentum, which anchor InP laser/device capacity. The underfollowed lane includes Fabrinet as a manufacturing-capacity and optical assembly beneficiary, and Aeluma as a speculative alternative III-V-on-silicon platform that could matter if native InP capacity remains constrained. Evidence quality is uneven: COHR, LITE, and FN have more commercial exposure; ALMU remains a higher-risk hypothesis requiring proof of revenue conversion, qualified customers, and scalable yields.
